My Price is My Life | Setting Sail with Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley and James O’Keefe Episode #4

Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley comes aboard the Lucky Charm III to share what her life’s been like since she heroically exposed how the federal government was handling (and allegedly hiding) adverse reactions to the COVID-19 vaccine.

In 2021, Jodi was a nurse at the Phoenix Indian Medical Center, a facility under the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). She tells James how the Holy Spirit prompted her to hit “record” while her concerned colleagues, including physicians, were discussing patients they believed were suffering adverse effects from the vaccine, reactions that weren't being formally reported. Thus, igniting Jodi’s ongoing advocacy in nursing.

Jodi also shares other challenging moments in her life that strengthened her faith and trust in God, leading her to the work and mission she’s tackling now.

Thailand. From September 15, visa-free stay is 30 days again, not 60

The special 60-day regime that was granted to citizens of about 93 countries since July 2024 is being cancelled. The new rules will start from September 15, 2026. Until this date, 60 days are still given at the border.

What's changing:
• Most countries, including Russia, USA, EU, UK, Australia - visa-free stay of 30 days.
• Seychelles and Mauritius - 15 days.
• Visa on Arrival is being limited; countries like Azerbaijan, Belarus, Serbia remain on the list.
• Those already in the country on a 60-day stamp can complete their stay. There is no retroactive effect.
• DTV, LTR, Privilege, work, pension - remain unchanged.

Why: in May, the government decided to close the gap for visa-runners, nominal tourists, and those living in the country for months. The usual package vacation (~9 days) is almost unaffected.
For Russians, the visa-free stay is not being canceled - they are simply returning to the old 30-day limit under a bilateral agreement.
